question: Is there a strategy that, run only in CHOP-labelled regimes with the trend core elsewhere, beats trend-only in both halves of history?
registration_note: Declared 2026-09-27 before any candidate result. Six candidates with textbook or a-priori parameters are all reported; any pass is a forward hypothesis, not a finding.
book: TREND/MIXED -> frozen DON8+EMA8 core target; CHOP -> candidate target; UNKNOWN -> flat

candidates.C1_bb_meanrev: bb_mean_reversion 20/2.0, RSI14 30/70, max_hold 20 (reference; failed in regime-switch-v1)
candidates.C2_zscore_reversal: intraday_reversal lookback 3 bars (1 day), z 1.5, exit |z|<0.15, max_hold 6
candidates.C3_squeeze_breakout: bb_squeeze_breakout 20/2.0, squeeze_q 0.2 over 200 bars, exit at mid, max_hold 40
candidates.C4_trend_pullback: trend_pullback EMA 24/96, RSI14 long<40 short>60, exit on EMA cross, max_hold 30
candidates.C5_xs_reversal: among CHOP coins each bar: long 3 worst, short 3 best 3-bar returns (market neutral)
candidates.C6_funding_carry: hold the funding-receiving side when |3-day per-8h funding| > 0.01%

comparators.chop_flat: core outside CHOP, flat in CHOP

economics.funding: Binance USDT-M proxy, charged to every book
economics.sizing: entry inverse-vol 15% per sleeve, cap 1, 180 bars

pass_rule: combined-book Sharpe > trend_only Sharpe in BOTH halves; reported alongside full-period Sharpe and the candidate's own CHOP-only mean
multiplicity_note: 6 candidates: with no real effect about 1.5 would beat trend_only in both halves by chance if halves were independent coin flips, so a pass is a forward hypothesis only
